en: The Sūtra on the Great Powerful Vidyārāja Samantāloka, Who Gives Birth to the Dharma-Eye of All Tathāgatas, Spoken by the Buddha. Scroll One.
Translated at Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India, in the Kingdom of the Western Heaven.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa and Subject Fa-hu, by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavān was staying on Mount Mahāmucilinda.
Within the great jewel pavilion, he preached the Dharma for the assembly.
At that time, all the Buddhas extolled and praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi.
Thereupon, that assembly all came together and took their seats.
They sat at the very first position on the eastern side of the World-Honored One’s lotus throne, which was universally ablaze with garlands of flames.
The Buddha then comforted the sentient beings with his right hand.
Next, to the right of the Buddha, is the Four-Armed Mahābalavīra Vidyārāja.
His left hand is raised in salutation toward the Buddha’s crown;
his right hand holds a fly-whisk (*cāmara*); and his upper left hand holds a vajra-noose (*vajrapāśa*).
In his upper right hand, he holds a vajra-staff.
His eyes are vermilion and his hair is like blazing fire, rising upward in flames.
Next is Vajrapāṇi together with his retinue.
Next, on the right side is the Vidyārāja Trailokyavijaya,
and on the left side is Amṛtakuṇḍalin;
their forms are like half-moons, displaying vigorous and fierce majesty.
His appearance is hideous and his color is vermilion-red.
This Great Terrifying Vajra is able to shatter all afflictions and the firm attachments of the fundamental mind.
Next is the Noble Trailokyavijaya Vidyārāja,
the Noble Māmakī, and Amṛtakuṇḍalī.
The Vajrāṅkuśa and the Vajrapāśa;
within those gates, there are further two wrathful vajras,
the left one holding a vajra-mallet.
To the right, he holds a vajra-staff.
Next, to the Buddha’s left, is the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara together with his retinue.
Next, to the Buddha’s right, is the Noble Pāṇḍaravāsinī Avalokiteśvara.
As well as the Bodhisattva Tārā,
the Bodhisattva Bhṛkuṭī,
and on the left side, the Vidyārāja Hayagrīva.
Next were Mahāśvetā, Mañjuśrī,
and other such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas numbering in the hundreds of thousands;
furthermore, there were the sun and moon deities from the eastern direction and others.
The Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Śakra Devendra,
Yama and the Fire God of the southeast, together with all the great ṛṣis.
In the south is Yamuna and Nārāyaṇa;
in the southwest is the Lord of Rākṣasas;
in the west is Varuṇa, the Lord of Nāgas.
In the northwest is Vāyu; in the north, Kuvēra;
and in the northeast, Īśāna.
Śakra Devānām Indra,
Nārāyaṇa, and Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World.
The host of devaputras headed by Maheśvara,
as well as these and other immeasurable and innumerable pure devas and devaputras,
each surrounded by their own retinues.
Before the Tathāgata, they joined their palms in reverence and gazed up at his venerable countenance.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Lord of Secrets, Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Lord of Secrets, if there should be one who upholds this Great Teaching, the Sūtra of the Vidyārāja..."
He spoke the mantra, saying:
*Namo ratnatrayāya, namo ākhaṇḍavajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpataye, oṃ kili kili vajra kīlaya svāhā; oṃ mārīcanāya svāhā; rāraṭaya svāhā.*

One should install the Great Powerful Vidyārāja within the maṇḍala.
Then, performing visualization, one should secretly perform the protection.
Next, one should take refuge in and pay homage to the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha.
The Pratyekabuddhas, the Elder Śāriputra, the assembly of śrāvakas,
and all the great bodhisattvas such as Maitreya— homage to you!
We prostrate to the Perfectly Awakened One, the Fully Enlightened Buddha.
I take refuge in the Vajradhara and his retinue.
Furthermore, he spoke this mantra: Tadyathā...

ṛḍara hāri hari kucī kucī cina cina pīna pīna sarvauṣṭhānāṃ guṃ muṃ guṃ muṃ hara.

Rya pradyumna-pāveṅ nṛpu nṛpu nṛpu nṛpu namo vajradharāya sarvavara-siddhi-damanapānine.
*Svāhā | Namaḥ vajradharāya mahātejase svāhā | Oṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* This vidyārāja constantly provides secret protection through his majestic power.
All that was to be done was fully accomplished.
At that time, Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha,
immediately emitted everywhere the pure radiance of a flaming garland.
It illuminated the trichiliocosm,
incinerating all the palaces of the Māra kings;
with blazing flames surrounding it as a single mass of fire, it consumed and swept away everything without remainder.
At that time, the Māra King, by the power of his own karma, refused to submit.
Those various Māra kings and their demonic hosts then gave rise to malice and became individually enraged.
Holding various weapons such as sharp swords, bows, arrows, and discuses,
the Lord of Secrets Vajrapāṇi appeared just as the Buddha had manifested,
having traveled past worlds as numerous as the sands of twenty-one Ganges Rivers to the east.
All the Māra kings were completely subdued.
His body was crimson and his eyes were azure; four fangs protruded from his mouth.
He knit his brows and glared with bared teeth; his hair stood upright like vermilion.
Possessing great majesty and power, his right hand holds a staff and his left hand holds a vajra;
he is adorned with dragons and wears a tiger-skin garment.
In this same manner, in the south, west, and north,
he likewise manifested his body in as many worlds as there are grains of sand in twenty-one Ganges Rivers, subduing them all.
At that time, countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of malevolent Māras were subdued by the Great Powerful Vidyārāja Ucchuṣma.
Terrified, trembling, and panicked with confusion,
his four limbs became powerless and he lost all sensory perception;
disregarding his own life, he was bound by the fivefold fetters of the King of Māra’s own karma.
When the Lord of Mysteries, Vajrapāṇi, had performed these deeds,
there immediately appeared the hosts of the Yama devas, the Tuṣita devas, the Nirmāṇarati devas, and the Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas.
Each carrying various kinds of ointments and incense,
as well as many exquisite flowers, banners, flags, silken canopies, and parasols,
they went to the place where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni was and made offerings.
Having circumambulated the Buddha to the right, they withdrew and sat to one side.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
having offered praise and eulogy for all the Tathāgatas, [remained there].
Within the most supreme and great teaching, the Tathāgata’s great wisdom has brought forth all the mantras of immeasurable majesty,
heroic power, and great strength that grant mastery over all that is sought according to one's wishes.
Desiring to bring benefit, welfare, and happiness to all sentient beings in the heavens and among humans, he then spoke this mantra:
*Oṃ vajrakrodha mahā-māra-hana hana bhasma kuru vidhvaṃsaya jvala jvala mānaraudrakrodha hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi...
He addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One,
if there are good men or good women who,
upon hearing this True Dharma, receive, uphold, read, recite, and extensively explain it to others."
With diligent perseverance and respectful offerings,
one shall receive empowerment within all maṇḍalas and obtain this mantra; by means of it,
one will immediately be able to subjugate and destroy all incantations.
At that time, the Lord of Secrets Vajrapāṇi again addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
the Buddha has spoken this Heart Dhāraṇī of the Great Power Vidyārāja."
If anyone upholds this,
they will immediately obtain those yakṣas and the hosts of yakṣas,
as well as the rākṣasas and the hosts of rākṣasas.
The Gaṇas of Kiñjika and Kiñjika,
and the Gaṇas of Garuḍa and Garuḍa,
each made solemn vows to provide protection and support.
Furthermore, there were nāga kings, gandharvas, piśācas, uḍḍāmara-s, and nākinīs.
Satsya-sa-khila, kopa-samāra, kaṭhabuttana.
Maitraṇa and all such others—
this entire host of evil names and terrifying beings,
along with their retinues, shall be unable to cause harm.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, Lord of Secrets, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! Out of great compassion, you extensively perform the Buddha-work for the sake of all sentient beings."
Then the Lord of Secrets, Vajrapāṇi, addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, if there should be those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra,
and who remember it without forgetting and extensively explain it to others..."
That person shall immediately attain liberation from saṃsāra; those who behold him will joyfully offer worship and prostrations.
Then Vajrapāṇi again spoke the mantra of Immeasurable Heroic Power.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ ghorasūrapāṇi hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ.
Oṃ sujati niṃ na na hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ namo mahāvalāya svāhā | oṃ jvala jvala sa...
ṛvauṣṭha saṃpāya saṃpāya.
Nurāḥ joṣṭhaṃ nivāraya mama sarvasattvānām.

Ṭa oṃ vajra-krodha mahāvala kiṃkara kiṃkara naśaya naśaya. [This mantra] is to be kept secret at all times for the purpose of protection.
If there are those who receive, uphold, read, and recite this dhāraṇī,
they will be able to subdue even celestial fires;
the dead shall be restored to life, and they will be able to withstand hostile māras.
One shall also obtain whatever children one seeks.
By reciting this dhāraṇī over a single handful of water and sprinkling it upon the ground,
one can neutralize all poisons of snakes, scorpions, and the like.
Those who are pregnant shall all attain peace and security, free from all suffering and affliction.
All their undertakings shall be accomplished,
and all mantras shall likewise be efficacious.
Those who are able to receive and uphold this sūtra shall attain great peace and happiness.
At that time, Īśānabhūti, the lord of countless koṭis of devas,
surrounded by his own retinue, arose within that maṇḍala and prostrated at the feet of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi said:
"Noble One, you have now spoken for our sake this Great Power Amoghasiddhi Dhāraṇī of Immeasurable Heroic Strength."
We love and delight in it;
even the Brahmā kings, Śakra, the devas, and the asuras pay it homage and prostrate themselves. Yakṣa, rākṣasa, and vetāla.
Kaṭapūtana, Ūnamasi! Cause them all to be terrified;
subdue that host by either beating or killing them.
The door bolts and locks shall fall away and be destroyed without remainder.
This Maṇḍala King is capable of accomplishing all manner of diverse activities.
At that time, those multitudes...
He praised and extolled Bhūtādhipati, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Bhūtādhipati!
You have been able to question the Tathāgata, the Vajradhara, on behalf of all sentient beings."
At that time, the World-Honored One Vajrapāṇi cast the wheel of mastery of the vajra-pestle;
immediately, that vajra swiftly descended and remained within that vajra-lotus.
He immediately entered the yoga-contemplation.
All the hosts of the maṇḍala beheld the Great Wrathful One,
his countenance majestic and terrifying, with venomous snakes covering his entire body.
If one wishes to subdue and overcome all the hosts of māras within that maṇḍala,
one should enter this samādhi,
namely, the samādhi of great compassion for all sentient beings.
The Samādhi of Universal Radiance;
the Samādhi of Joyful Vision of Dharmas;
the Samādhi of Manifesting All the Realms of Māra Kings.
The Seal Samādhi; the Samādhi Manifesting the Lands of All Sentient Beings;
the Immovable Samādhi.
The samādhi of love for the Dharma;
the samādhi of the manifestation of all dharmas;
the samādhi of great power.
Upon entering such samādhis, as he was about to enter,
countless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Māra kings spontaneously gave rise to terror;
they saw themselves bound by the Great Powerful Vidyārāja.
He immediately wailed aloud with a great cry, as if the fire at the end of an eon were burning his own body and his life was not far off.
He then went to the place where the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi resided.
He addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Noble One, I pray that you will look upon me with compassion and protect me.
World-Honored One, I am in extreme suffering."
"The Great Powerful Vidyārāja has bound me;
he lashes and torments me, and my life hangs by a thread. I pray that you will grant me protection.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi arose from that samādhi.
He addressed all the fourfold assemblies within the maṇḍala, saying these words:
"This supreme, great merit, great majestic power, and great wrathful one is thus, thus."
World-Honored One, this is great merit, this is great majestic power, this is great wrath.
This is the *Sūtra on the Great Power King Vidyārāja Samantāloka, the Dharma-Eye Born from All Tathāgatas*, Volume One, spoken by the Buddha.
Spoken by the Buddha, the *Sūtra on the Great Power King Vidyārāja Samantāloka, the Dharma-Eye Born from All Tathāgatas*.
The *Bala-vajrapāṇi-tantra*, Scroll II,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master, the Imperially Ennobled Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Dharma-pāla,
a subject of the Kingdom of Magadha in Central India, at Nālandā Monastery, by imperial decree. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi looked back toward the assembly within the maṇḍala.
With eyes like those of a lion and possessing sovereign majestic power,
he expounded the ritual of the Maṇḍala of the Great Powerful Vidyārāja for Īśāna, the lord of the Bhūtas,
saying: "Noble One, if there should be anyone who enters this maṇḍala of great wrath..."
One will immediately be able to accomplish all undertakings and shall not meet with untimely death.
One will remain far removed from all evil diseases that afflict the body and will not be born into the realm of Māra.
All sentient beings who see one will rejoice.
Furthermore, one will be able to distance oneself from all enemies;
subsequently, all mantra teachings will be fully accomplished,
and one will also be able to achieve mastery over all wrathful deities.
Because one attains the merit of all consecrations, there is auspicious adornment.
At that time, first arrange this great maṇḍala of the wrathful deity;
by reciting this sūtra ten thousand times, one will attain a state of excellence.
Having beheld this maṇḍala and received the master’s authorization,
one may then study the ritual procedures for this mantra-maṇḍala;
first, one must abstain from food for eight days.
By taking refuge in the Triple Gem and generating the bodhicitta of great compassion,
